The template handler avoids that stall by capturing the request, immediately returning a synthetic successful response, and sending the real request asynchronously through a Polly resilience pipeline.\\n\\nOpenTelemetry added task-based batch and metric workers for single-threaded WebAssembly in open-telemetry/opentelemetry-dotnet#6379, but the worker still invokes the synchronous exporter contract. The remaining limitation is tracked by open-telemetry/opentelemetry-dotnet#7708.\\n\\nOnce that issue is resolved and the fix is available in a stable OpenTelemetry release, remove the template workaround and use the standard OTLP exporter implementation.\\n\\n### Proposed changes\\n\\n- Update the Blazor WebAssembly Service Defaults OpenTelemetry dependencies to a stable version containing the fix for open-telemetry/opentelemetry-dotnet#7708.\\n- Delete `BackgroundExportHandler.cs`.\\n- Remove the custom `IPostConfigureOptions` configuration that supplies `BackgroundExportHandler`.\\n- Remove the custom `ResiliencePipelineBuilder` configuration.\\n- Remove the `Microsoft.Extensions.Http.Resilience` dependency if it is no longer otherwise needed.\\n- Configure logs, traces, and metrics using the standard `AddOtlpExporter` APIs.\\n- Allow OTLP exporters to use the normal HTTP client integration without bypassing globally configured asynchronous handlers such as service discovery.\\n\\n### Validation\\n\\nAdd or update browser integration coverage to verify that, in single-threaded Blazor WebAssembly:\\n\\n- Logs, traces, and metrics are exported successfully over OTLP/HTTP.\\n- Export works when `IHttpClientFactory` includes an asynchronous delegating handler, including the globally configured service-discovery handler used by the template.\\n- Export requests are not reported as successful before the HTTP operation completes.\\n- Export failures are surfaced through normal OpenTelemetry diagnostics.\\n- Retry, timeout, flush, and shutdown behavior use OpenTelemetry\\u0026#39;s standard semantics without fire-and-forget requests.\\n- No provider must be manually resolved to initialize OpenTelemetry; normal `IHostedService` startup remains sufficient.\\n\\n### Dependencies\\n\\nBlocked by:\\n\\n- open-telemetry/opentelemetry-dotnet#7708\\n\\nRelated:\\n\\n- #64574\\n- #64890\\n- #67259\\n- #67267\\n\",\"state\":\"open\",\"html_url\":\"https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/issues/68801\",\"user\":{\"login\":\"danroth27\",\"id\":1874516,\"profile_url\":\"https://github.com/danroth27\",\"avatar_url\":\"https://avatars.githubusercontent.com/u/1874516?v=4\"},\"author_association\":\"MEMBER\",\"labels\":[\"area-blazor\"],\"comments\":1,\"reactions\":{\"total_count\":0,\"+1\":0,\"-1\":0,\"laugh\":0,\"confused\":0,\"heart\":0,\"hooray\":0,\"rocket\":0,\"eyes\":0},\"created_at\":\"2026-08-26T11:52:00Z\",\"updated_at\":\"2026-08-26T11:56:38Z\",\"issue_type\":\"Feature\",\"has_parent\":false,\"has_children\":false,\"closed_by_pull_requests\":{\"total_count\":0,\"references\":[]}}"}],"resultType":"complete"}}

For example:\\n\\n50 / 50 = 100%\\n50 / 51 = 98%\\n\\nThis results in the visible progress changing from 100% back to 98%, which\\nlooks broken and unprofessional to users.\\n\\nExpected behavior:\\n\\n- The total number of startup resources should be fixed before progress is reported.\\n- Progress must never decrease.\\n- 100% must only be reported after all required startup resources are loaded.\\n- Ideally, progress should represent downloaded bytes instead of only a resource count.\\n\\nPlease treat this as a correctness bug in the built-in Blazor loading indicator,\\nnot only as a feature request.\\n\\n### Expected Behavior\\n\\nThe built-in Blazor WebAssembly loading progress must be monotonic.\\n\\nOnce the progress reaches 100%, it must never decrease again. The value 100% should only be reported after all startup resources have been discovered and loaded.\\n\\n### Steps To Reproduce\\n\\n\\n\\n\\n    \\n    \\n    \\n\\n    \\n\\n\\n    \\n        \\u003cp\\u003e\\u003c/p\\u003e\\n    \\n\\n    \\n\\n    \\n\\n\\n\\n\\n\\n1. Create a standard Blazor WebAssembly application.\\n2. Replace the contents of wwwroot/index.html with the code above.\\n3. Publish and serve the application.\\n4. Open the browser developer console.\\n5. Reload the page.\\n\\nThe observer records all changes to Blazor\\u0026#39;s\\n--blazor-load-percentage CSS variable.\\n\\nOn the affected production application, the observed sequence included:\\n\\n87.74% -\\u0026gt; 100% -\\u0026gt; 96.30% -\\u0026gt; 99.38% -\\u0026gt; 100%\\n\\nThe browser console reports \\u0026#34;Progress decreased\\u0026#34; when the value moves\\nbackwards after already reaching 100%.\\n\\n### Exceptions (if any)\\n\\n_No response_\\n\\n### .NET Version\\n\\nNETCoreApp,Version=v10.0\\n\\n### Anything else?\\n\\n    \\u0026#34;name\\u0026#34;: \\u0026#34;.NETCoreApp,Version=v10.0\\u0026#34;,\",\"state\":\"open\",\"html_url\":\"https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/issues/67979\",\"user\":{\"login\":\"RoellinRacing\",\"id\":154523119,\"profile_url\":\"https://github.com/RoellinRacing\",\"avatar_url\":\"https://avatars.githubusercontent.com/u/154523119?v=4\"},\"author_association\":\"NONE\",\"labels\":[\"area-blazor\"],\"reactions\":{\"total_count\":1,\"+1\":1,\"-1\":0,\"laugh\":0,\"confused\":0,\"heart\":0,\"hooray\":0,\"rocket\":0,\"eyes\":0},\"created_at\":\"2026-07-23T12:16:30Z\",\"updated_at\":\"2026-08-26T06:27:27Z\",\"issue_type\":\"Bug\",\"has_parent\":false,\"has_children\":false,\"closed_by_pull_requests\":{\"total_count\":0,\"references\":[]}}"}],"resultType":"complete"}}

This is noted in the code already:\\n\\nhttps://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/blob/[REDACTED]/src/Hosting/Hosting/src/Internal/HostingApplicationDiagnostics.cs#L462-L466\\n\\nTo properly implement the specification, some sort of configuration surface needs to be designed to allow it to be configured and have sensible built-in defaults for redaction.\\n\\nSee #64850 and #65369.\\n\\nThere\\u0026#39;s some prior art for implementing this also in the HttpClient instrumentation for the `url.full` attribute ([`DiagnosticsHandler.SendAsyncCore()`](https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/[REDACTED]/src/libraries/System.Net.Http/src/System/Net/Http/DiagnosticsHandler.cs#L132) and [`UriRedactionHelper`](https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/[REDACTED]/src/libraries/Common/src/System/Net/Http/UriRedactionHelper)).\\n\\n---\\n\\nThe second is support for providing a way to override the list of known values for `http.request.method`. For example, the `OTEL_INSTRUMENTATION_HTTP_KNOWN_METHODS` is one way of doing this. This would also require a configuration surface needs to be designed to allow it to be configured and have sensible built-in defaults for redaction.\\n\\nThe second could be argued to be optional if HTTP QUERY is fully supported (see #63276, #65489, #65714).\\n\\nThere was a similar discussion around that for HttpClient\\u0026#39;s instrumentation, and they decided to not implement it: https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/issues/123936#issuecomment-4083898523\\n\\n### Expected Behavior\\n\\nASP.NET Core 11 implements all (conditionally) required parts of the OpenTelemetry [Semantic Validate the `IAntiforgeryValidationFeature` on the request before reading from the form.\\n```\\nThis can be fixed by disabling AntiForgery on the endpoint, but we are not sure if this is correct?\\n- After x amount of time, it seems like the frontend \\u0026#39;forgets\\u0026#39; your authentication. All the [Authorize] attributes return an unauthorized, and getting items from the claims `await AuthenticationStateProvider.GetAuthenticationStateAsync();` returns nothing.\\n\\n**To Reproduce**\\n\\nSteps to reproduce the behavior:\\n\\n1. Adjust the BlazorWebAppOidcBffAuto sample to only be InteractiveWebAssembly.\\n2. Deploy the application through: `dotnet publish \\u0026#34;${PROJECT}.csproj\\u0026#34; -c Release -p RuntimeIdentifier=linux-x64`\\n3. Try to authentication/logout endpoint.\\n\\n**Additional context**\\n\\n- DOTNET 10\\n- Template: https://github.com/dotnet/blazor-samples/tree/main/10.0/BlazorWebAppOidcBffAuto\\n\\nIs InteractiveWebAssembly not supported with the sample codes, or there any different changes we need to do?\\n\\n(cc: @guardrex https://github.com/dotnet/blazor-samples/issues/642)\",\"state\":\"open\",\"html_url\":\"https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/issues/65368\",\"user\":{\"login\":\"Schoof-T\",\"id\":2319986,\"profile_url\":\"https://github.com/Schoof-T\",\"avatar_url\":\"https://avatars.githubusercontent.com/u/2319986?v=4\"},\"author_association\":\"NONE\",\"labels\":[\"area-auth\",\"Needs: Attention :wave:\",\"Needs: Repro\"],\"milestone\":\"Backlog\",\"comments\":6,\"reactions\":{\"total_count\":0,\"+1\":0,\"-1\":0,\"laugh\":0,\"confused\":0,\"heart\":0,\"hooray\":0,\"rocket\":0,\"eyes\":0},\"created_at\":\"2026-02-09T12:00:32Z\",\"updated_at\":\"2026-08-19T07:44:43Z\",\"has_parent\":false,\"has_children\":false,\"closed_by_pull_requests\":{\"total_count\":0,\"references\":[]}}"}],"resultType":"complete"}}

This is a problem for me because my website is for New Zealand and Australia and so all the date inputs format, so `InvariantCulture` will incorrectly deserialize the `DateTime` values.\\n\\nIn MVC there\\u0026#39;s similar issues, but I can create a custom implementation of `IModelBinderProvider` so I can fix it, but the relevant types here are all internal, like `FormDataConverter`, `FormDataConverter` , `ISingleValueConverter` and `FormDataMapperOptions`.  If they where public I could create my own implementation and configure `FormDataMapperOptions` to add them.\\n\\nAnother approach I tried was to create my own implementation of `SupplyParameterFromFormAttribute`. From there there\\u0026#39;s lots of approaches I could take, possibly something crazy like wrapping some calls to `IModelBinderFactory` so my MVC and Blazor code could share serialization behavior, but that\\u0026#39;s not possible either because `ICascadingValueSupplier` is also internal.\\n\\n## Proposed API\\n\\nSo I\\u0026#39;d like to propose making `ICascadingValueSupplier` public, and either making `FormDataConverter` and `ISingleValueConverter` public, or creating a new interface to implement so `FormDataReader` doesn\\u0026#39;t need to be exposed publicly also.\\n\\n## Usage Examples\\n\\n### Custom FormDataConverter\\n\\n```csharp\\nvar builder = WebApplication.CreateBuilder(args);\\n\\nbuilder.Services.Configure(options =\\u0026gt;\\n{\\n    options.Converters[typeof(DateTime)] = new CustomDateTimeConverter();\\n});\\n\\ninternal class CustomDateTimeConverter : FormDataConverter, ISingleValueConverter\\n{\\n    private static CultureInfo NZCulture = new CultureInfo(\\u0026#34;en-NZ\\u0026#34;);\\n\\n    public bool CanConvertSingleValue() =\\u0026gt; true;\\n\\n    public bool TryConvertValue(ref FormDataReader reader, string value, out DateTime result)\\n    {\\n        if (DateTime.TryParse(value, NZCulture.DateTimeFormat, out result!))\\n            return true;\\n        else\\n            return false;\\n    }\\n\\n    internal override bool TryRead(ref FormDataReader reader, Type type, FormDataMapperOptions options, out DateTime result, out bool found)\\n    {\\n        found = reader.TryGetValue(out var value);\\n        if (!found)\\n        {\\n            result = default;\\n            return true;\\n        }\\n        else\\n        {\\n            return TryConvertValue(ref reader, value!, out result!);\\n        }\\n    }\\n}\\n```\\n\\n### Custom SupplyParameterFromFormAttribute\\n\\n``` csharp\\npublic static class CustomSupplyParameterFromFormServiceCollectionExtensions\\n{\\n    public static IServiceCollection AddCustomSupplyValueFromFormProvider(this IServiceCollection serviceCollection)\\n    {\\n        serviceCollection.AddScoped();\\n\\n        return serviceCollection;\\n    }\\n}\\n\\n\\n[AttributeUsage(AttributeTargets.Property, AllowMultiple = false, Inherited = true)]\\npublic class CustomSupplyParameterFromFormAttribute : CascadingParameterAttributeBase\\n{\\n}\\n\\ninternal class CustomSupplyParameterFromFormValueProvider : ICascadingValueSupplier\\n{\\n    private readonly IModelMetadataProvider _metadataProvider;\\n    private readonly FormMappingContext _mappingContext;\\n    private readonly IModelBinderFactory _modelBinderFactory;\\n    private readonly IFormValueMapper? _formValueMapper;\\n\\n    public CustomSupplyParameterFromFormValueProvider(IFormValueMapper? formValueMapper, IModelMetadataProvider metadataProvider, IModelBinderFactory modelBinderFactory)\\n    {\\n        _metadataProvider = metadataProvider;\\n        _mappingContext = new FormMappingContext(\\u0026#34;\\u0026#34;);\\n        _modelBinderFactory = modelBinderFactory;\\n        _formValueMapper = formValueMapper;\\n    }\\n\\n    bool ICascadingValueSupplier.IsFixed =\\u0026gt; true;\\n\\n    public bool CanSupplyValue(in CascadingParameterInfo parameterInfo)\\n    {\\n        if (_formValueMapper is not null \\u0026amp;\\u0026amp; parameterInfo.Attribute is CustomSupplyParameterFromFormAttribute)\\n            return _formValueMapper.CanMap(parameterInfo.PropertyType, \\u0026#34;\\u0026#34;, \\u0026#34;\\u0026#34;);\\n\\n        return false;\\n    }\\n\\n    public object? GetCurrentValue(object? key, in CascadingParameterInfo parameterInfo)\\n    {\\n        var modelMetadata = _metadataProvider.GetMetadataForType(parameterInfo.PropertyType);\\n\\n        var valueProvider = new FormMappingContextValueProvider(_mappingContext);\\n\\n        var actionContext = new ActionContext()\\n        {\\n            HttpContext = new DefaultHttpContext(),\\n            RouteData = new Microsoft.AspNetCore.Routing.RouteData(),\\n            ActionDescriptor = new Microsoft.AspNetCore.Mvc.Abstractions.ActionDescriptor()\\n        };\\n\\n        var modelBindingContext = DefaultModelBindingContext.CreateBindingContext(\\n            actionContext,\\n            valueProvider,\\n            modelMetadata,\\n            bindingInfo: null,\\n            modelName: string.Empty);\\n\\n        var result = modelMetadata.ModelType.IsValueType ? Activator.CreateInstance(modelMetadata.ModelType) : null;\\n\\n        modelBindingContext.Model = result;\\n\\n        var factoryContext = new ModelBinderFactoryContext()\\n        {\\n            Metadata = modelMetadata,\\n            BindingInfo = new BindingInfo()\\n            {\\n                BinderModelName = modelMetadata.BinderModelName,\\n                BinderType = modelMetadata.BinderType,\\n                BindingSource = modelMetadata.BindingSource,\\n                PropertyFilterProvider = modelMetadata.PropertyFilterProvider,\\n            },\\n\\n            CacheToken = modelMetadata,\\n        };\\n\\n        var binder = _modelBinderFactory.CreateBinder(factoryContext);\\n\\n        binder.BindModelAsync(modelBindingContext).Wait();\\n\\n        if (modelBindingContext.ModelState.Count \\u0026gt; 0)\\n            return result;\\n\\n        return default;\\n    }\\n\\n    void ICascadingValueSupplier.Subscribe(ComponentState subscriber, in CascadingParameterInfo parameterInfo)\\n        =\\u0026gt; throw new NotSupportedException(); // IsFixed = true, so the framework won\\u0026#39;t call this\\n\\n    void ICascadingValueSupplier.Unsubscribe(ComponentState subscriber, in CascadingParameterInfo parameterInfo)\\n        =\\u0026gt; throw new NotSupportedException(); // IsFixed = true, so the framework won\\u0026#39;t call this\\n}\\n```\\n\\n## Alternative Designs\\n\\nI think there\\u0026#39;s a lot of ways that these could be done, new interfaces so not so many internals are exposed.\\n\\n## Risks\\n\\nI\\u0026#39;m unsure about how the internals of the form deserialization full works, especially when enhanced navigation is involved, so exposing these things might be much more complicated than I think, and it could be too complex to allow people to create their own implantations that don\\u0026#39;t break things entirely\",\"state\":\"open\",\"html_url\":\"https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/issues/66731\",\"user\":{\"login\":\"neoGeneva\",\"id\":804724,\"profile_url\":\"https://github.com/neoGeneva\",\"avatar_url\":\"https://avatars.githubusercontent.com/u/804724?v=4\"},\"author_association\":\"NONE\",\"labels\":[\"area-blazor\",\"api-suggestion\",\"area...

Unlike launching directly from Visual Studio or via `dotnet run`, the Aspire dashboard launches the app by opening a URL in the default browser without the necessary debugging flags.\\n\\n## Current Behavior\\n\\n- Aspire dashboard provides a clickable link that opens the app in the default browser\\n- No debugging capabilities are available\\n- Developers must manually restart the browser with remote debugging flags to debug\\n\\n## Expected Behavior\\n\\nThe Aspire dashboard should provide an option to:\\n1. Allow seamless debugging experience similar to F5 debugging in Visual Studio\\n\\n## Possible Solutions\\n\\n1. **Add a \\u0026#34;Debug\\u0026#34; button** next to the app URL in the dashboard that launches the browser with debugging enabled\\n2. **Provide launch settings integration** that respects debugging configuration from launchSettings.json\\n3. **Automatic debugger attachment** when the app is launched in debug mode via Aspire\\n\\n## Additional Context\\n\\nThis is particularly important for:\\n- Developers working with Aspire-orchestrated applications\\n- Teams debugging complex multi-project solutions\\n- Testing debugging scenarios in containerized environments\\n\\n## Related Issues\\n\\n- Part of improving Aspire developer experience\\n- Related to general Blazor WebAssembly debugging workflows\",\"state\":\"open\",\"state_reason\":\"reopened\",\"html_url\":\"https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/issues/64891\",\"user\":{\"login\":\"javiercn\",\"id\":6995051,\"profile_url\":\"https://github.com/javiercn\",\"avatar_url\":\"https://avatars.githubusercontent.com/u/6995051?v=4\"},\"author_association\":\"MEMBER\",\"labels\":[\"area-blazor\",\"on-roadmap\"],\"assignees\":[\"maraf\"],\"milestone\":\"Backlog\",\"comments\":3,\"reactions\":{\"total_count\":6,\"+1\":6,\"-1\":0,\"laugh\":0,\"confused\":0,\"heart\":0,\"hooray\":0,\"rocket\":0,\"eyes\":0},\"created_at\":\"2025-12-29T18:32:49Z\",\"updated_at\":\"2026-07-24T10:45:11Z\",\"has_parent\":true,\"has_children\":false,\"parent\":{\"number\":64888,\"title\":\"[Blazor] Aspire integration improvements\",\"state\":\"OPEN\",\"url\":\"https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/issues/64888\",\"repository\":\"dotnet/aspnetcore\"},\"closed_by_pull_requests\":{\"total_count\":0,\"references\":[]}}"}],"resultType":"complete"}}

The .NET/JS interop can continue using shared memory if we find it\\u0026#39;s necessary to have good perf on those older browsers (and thread safety is not difficult because it\\u0026#39;s all synchronous).\\n * **In a web worker (background thread) on more up-to-date browsers**. The .NET/JS interop will need to work by serializing any data that is being transferred rather than passing pointers [1].\\n\\nThis will be advantageous because then, even if your .NET code does something that locks up the CPU (such as a GC cycle), the UI will remain perfectly smooth (e.g., during animations or scrolling, or while the user is typing quickly into a textbox).\\n\\nThe existing UI update mechanism is designed around transferring batches of minimal diffs from .NET to JS, so it shouldn\\u0026#39;t be hugely difficult to have it express those diffs as serialized data rather than pointers into the WASM memory space. We\\u0026#39;ll have to be careful around things like event handling to ensure that the asynchrony can\\u0026#39;t result in inconsistency of behaviour versus the synchronous single-threaded model. For example, we will need to force all event delivery to be async as far as the JS side is concerned, even in the non-worker-thread case.\\n\\n*[1] Strictly speaking, we could also do it with shared memory on even newer browsers that support SharedArrayBuffer. But if we can get satisfactory perf without this, it would be better to serialize because it would mean fewer combinations of browser scenarios, and saves us having to deal with potentially complex thread-safety concerns on the .NET side.*\",\"state\":\"open\",\"state_reason\":\"reopened\",\"locked\":true,\"html_url\":\"https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/issues/5475\",\"user\":{\"login\":\"SteveSandersonMS\",\"id\":1101362,\"profile_url\":\"https://github.com/SteveSandersonMS\",\"avatar_url\":\"https://avatars.githubusercontent.com/u/1101362?v=4\"},\"author_association\":\"MEMBER\",\"labels\":[\"enhancement\",\"area-blazor\",\"severity-minor\",\"affected-very-few\",\"not-on-roadmap\"],\"assignees\":[\"pavelsavara\"],\"milestone\":\".NET 12 Planning\",\"comments\":14,\"reactions\":{\"total_count\":22,\"+1\":21,\"-1\":0,\"laugh\":0,\"confused\":0,\"heart\":0,\"hooray\":1,\"rocket\":0,\"eyes\":0},\"created_at\":\"2018-02-19T17:05:36Z\",\"updated_at\":\"2026-07-22T12:05:29Z\",\"issue_type\":\"Feature\",\"has_parent\":false,\"has_children\":false,\"closed_by_pull_requests\":{\"total_count\":1,\"references\":[{\"number\":67768,\"title\":\"Run Blazor WebAssembly in a Web Worker\",\"state\":\"CLOSED\",\"url\":\"https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/pull/67768\",\"repository\":\"dotnet/aspnetcore\"}]}}"}],"resultType":"complete"}}

In Blazor we use the .NET trimmer to significantly reduce the publish size of Blazor WebAssembly apps. However, we don\\u0026#39;t currently use the .NET trimmer to its fullest potential. We currently configure the trimmer in a partial mode, which only trims assemblies that are explicitly marked as trimmable. This typically means that the app assembly itself and many dependencies are not trimmed. This is a conservative setting that optimizes for maintaining functionality over reducing app size. \\n\\nThe default trim mode for the .NET trimmer is to trim everything. This is the mode used by the .NET Native AOT workloads.Analyzers provide warnings if there are code paths in the app that are not safe to trim. Given how sensitive web apps are to download size and load time, it seems like doing full trimming should be the goal for Blazor.\\n\\nEnabling support for full trimming also is a potential solution to enabling a [single project model for Blazor Web Apps](#49079) that target both server and browser. When you multitarget a project, everything in the project is built for both targets unless you indicated otherwise. This is problematic for browser scenarios because you may potentially bring in dependencies, components, and code into the browser targeted build that are only needed on the server. However, if we could enable full trimming *and* indicate to the trimmer which components are setup to render on WebAssembly, then the browser build could be aggressively trimmed to remove any unwanted code and dependencies.\\n\\nEnabling support for full .NET trimming typically means removing any dynamic code path that are based on reflection. We would need to make Blazor apps trimmer friendly by removing this code using techniques like source generators. For example, in Blazor we use reflection as part of the component discovery process and in the render tree builder code generated by the Razor compiler. We\\u0026#39;re already working on enabling [component discovery through source generation](https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/issues/48767). We also have on our backlog to [handle component parameters through source generation](https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/issues/29550). There may be other related work items as well.\\n\\nThere is also ecosystem impact of enabling full trimming by default. Many .NET libraries are not setup for trimming and would potentially need to be updated. It will take some time to work through these issues with the Blazor community. Certain features also simply wouldn\\u0026#39;t work with full trimming. For example, dynamically loading dependencies at runtime that are not known statically. For backwards compatibility, app developers can configure the trimmer to not trim assemblies that are not yet trimmer friendly. We\\u0026#39;d need to understand better all the cases that get impacted by full trimming and ensure we provide a reasonable user experience for addressing them.\",\"state\":\"open\",\"html_url\":\"https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/issues/49409\",\"user\":{\"login\":\"danroth27\",\"id\":1874516,\"profile_url\":\"https://github.com/danroth27\",\"avatar_url\":\"https://avatars.githubusercontent.com/u/1874516?v=4\"},\"author_association\":\"MEMBER\",\"labels\":[\"enhancement\",\"area-blazor\",\"Priority:1\",\"Pillar: Technical Debt\",\"feature-trimming\"],\"milestone\":\"Backlog\",\"comments\":20,\"reactions\":{\"total_count\":46,\"+1\":43,\"-1\":0,\"laugh\":0,\"confused\":0,\"heart\":0,\"hooray\":0,\"rocket\":0,\"eyes\":3},\"created_at\":\"2023-07-14T14:49:12Z\",\"updated_at\":\"2025-12-06T11:52:00Z\",\"issue_type\":\"Feature\",\"has_parent\":false,\"has_children\":false,\"closed_by_pull_requests\":{\"total_count\":0,\"references\":[]}}"}],"resultType":"complete"}}

[2026-08-26T22:05:44.390Z] [DEBUG] [rpc] github←resp 7092b {"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"result":{"_meta":{"io.modelcontextprotocol/serverInfo":{"icons":[{"mimeType":"image/png","src":"data:image/png;base64,","theme":"light"},{"mimeType":"image/png","src":"data:image/png;base64,","theme":"dark"}],"name":"github-mcp-server","title":"GitHub MCP Server","version":"v1.9.0"}},"content":[{"type":"text","text":"{\"number\":58811,\"title\":\"[Blazor] Improving ASP.NET Core integration\",\"body\":\"There are certain design choices in components that Blazor ships out of the box that make it hard to write applications that can work seamlessly on SSR scenarios and on interactive modes. This causes friction as there are many cases where the behavior is different on SSR and on Interactive sessions and developers have to account for both cases. Below is a non-exhaustive list of improvements that we can do to improve some of these experiences:\\n* Routing:\\n  * There are two routers, one on the server (ASP.NET Core) and one on the client. We\\u0026#39;ve merged the two implementations for the most part, but there are details that still cause confusion.\\n   * The need to declare additional assemblies in two locations: We should make the endpoint in ASP.NET Core pass along the configured assemblies to the client project via persisted state or some other mechanism.\\n   * Differences in handling `NotFound`: On SSR scenarios this is represented by an endpoint, on the interactive router with a `RenderFragment`. We should extend the router to take in a `NotFoundPage` parameter that can be used during SSR and Interactive rendering to display not found content.\\n   * Lack of `NavigationManager.NotFound()` or equivalent API for triggering `NotFound` on Blazor applications. This would trigger a 404 response on SSR scenarios that would render the `NotFound` page/component and on InteractiveScenarios it would signal any registered callback (the router) the equivalent situation (which would trigger the render).\\n   * Similar deal for triggering errors through an `Error` page.\\n * Authentication:\\n   * In ASP.NET Core you can use `Challenge` to trigger/start the authentication process. There is no Blazor equivalent for it, so users end up having to manually redirect users on interactive sessions.\\n   * We should extend `AuthenticationStateProvider` or similar APIs to support this type of scenario. On interactive sessions, a `Challenge` for a scheme will always result in a redirect (maybe challenge is not the right way to call this, and we should be using `RedirectToLogin` or some other verb. For server scenarios the information about the configured schemes is already available. For `WebAssembly` scenarios, information about the redirect URL can be provided via some mechanism like PersistedState. For schemes that need to generate additional information (like nonces, etc.) they\\u0026#39;ll be extended to add at least a new endpoint (maybe two) to handle the bootstrapping of the authentication process so that interactive clients (like webassembly) can redirect to a well-known URL to start the process.\\n* Lazy loading:\\n  * With prerendering, it can happen that we prerender a path that requires lazy loaded assemblies to render. The current APIs don\\u0026#39;t offer a way to make sure those assemblies are loaded before the page tries to render, which results in failures when the app goes interactive. We need:\\n  * A `LazyAssemblyLoader` implementation for prerendering (if you try to do this on any current .NET version it will fail).\\n  * For a given page, a list of all the dependent assemblies that are lazy loaded.\\n    * The ability to determine if they need to be immediately loaded for the page to render (for example, if the page references a type `B` that lives on a lazy loaded assembly on its `type definition` (`class A { public B BProp { get; set; } })` or if it can be delayed (because B is only used inside a method body).\\n  * A way to tell the runtime to load those assemblies when booting webassembly as we know they\\u0026#39;ll be needed immediately.\\n* Built-in components:\\n  * In general, we need to look at every component that we ship and ensure there\\u0026#39;s a way for them to work on each render mode in a reasonable way across render modes.\\n  * QuickGrid.\\n  * NavLink.\\n  * EditForm.\\n  * Section(s)\\n  * Cascading parameters.\",\"state\":\"open\",\"html_url\":\"https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/issues/58811\",\"user\":{\"login\":\"javiercn\",\"id\":6995051,\"profile_url\":\"https://github.com/javiercn\",\"avatar_url\":\"https://avatars.githubusercontent.com/u/6995051?v=4\"},\"author_association\":\"MEMBER\",\"labels\":[\"area-blazor\",\"Pillar: Dev Experience\"],\"milestone\":\"Backlog\",\"reactions\":{\"total_count\":5,\"+1\":0,\"-1\":0,\"laugh\":0,\"confused\":0,\"heart\":0,\"hooray\":0,\"rocket\":0,\"eyes\":5},\"created_at\":\"2024-11-06T09:38:38Z\",\"updated_at\":\"2025-08-26T13:05:35Z\",\"has_parent\":false,\"has_children\":true,\"sub_issues_summary\":{\"total\":7,\"completed\":4,\"percent_completed\":57},\"closed_by_pull_requests\":{\"total_count\":0,\"references\":[]}}"}],"resultType":"complete"}}

It is clear that this is a confusing aspect for customers and that they run into issues when they inadvertently introduce problematic patterns in their apps, like components rendering a large set of elements which can cause the memory to grow significantly.\\n\\nWhen a customer finds itself in this situation, they generally open an issue with us that suggest there is a memory leak in the framework (which has not been the case so far) and we get into a discussion where we explain how Blazor deals with circuits, how memory works in Server GC and how to troubleshoot memory issues. The general points that people miss are:\\n* Circuits are alive for a given time after the session ends (up to a maximum number of circuits) to support reconnection.\\n* The server will only collect the circuits when it triggers a collection for the generation they live in, and in general, they will tend to go to Gen2.\\n* Server GC will only trigger a Gen2 collection when the server is running low on memory.\\n\\nIt will be extremely helpful if we can add additional diagnostics to help bring visibility into some of the internal aspects of how Blazor server operates. Specifically:\\n* dotnet-counters to track on a given server instance over time:\\n  * The number of connected circuits.\\n  * The number of disconnected circuits.\\n\\nThis makes it trivial to prove that we are handling the circuit lifetime correctly (or to spot when we are not) and since all the allocated framework memory is rooted by a circuit, it makes it easy to prove that the memory issue is not on the framework.\\n\\nFurther diagnostics to help identify problematic circuit instances using clrMD to identify circuits consuming a large amount of memory. We can do this as follows:\\n* Attach to the live process (or a memory dump).\\n* Walk the heap to find all the CircuitHost instances.\\n* For each CircuitHost instance, introspect its renderer and look at the ComponentState instances.\\n* For each ComponentState, we look at the backing field for the CurrentRenderTree\\n* On the RenderTreeBuilder we look at RenderTreeFrameArrayBuilder we look at the _items field to check the length of the array as well as the `_itemsInUse`.\\n* With this information, we can point out when a component rendered a large number of elements in the past or is currently rendering a large number of elements.\\n  * If it is currently rendering a large number of elements, `_itemsInUse` will be large.\\n  * If it has rendered a large number of elements in the past `_items` will be large.\\n\\nWith this data, we should be able to point out what components rendered a large number of elements currently or in the past as well as what circuit they belong(ed) to and its current state (whether the circuit is active, disconnected, or waiting to be collected) and it should also help discard the framework or the component rendering as the source of the memory issues.\\n\\nNote that this could also be extended to use something similar to `!objsize` on a component instance to track how much memory that component is allocating, which in turn would help identify components in the app that are holding on to a lot of memory (think for example a component that has a large list in memory).\\n\\nThis last bit is not only useful for Blazor Server but it might be useful too for Blazor Webassembly and Desktop.\\n\\nAnother way to identify issues with the app this issue would be to check the `ArrayPool` to identify large buffers that might have been allocated by the app in the past.\\n\\nExamples of issues in this area in the past (there are likely more):\\nhttps://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/issues/43221\\nhttps://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/issues/39238\\nhttps://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/issues/39156\\nhttps://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/issues/33547\\nhttps://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/issues/33077\\nhttps://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/issues/32588\\nhttps://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/issues/30210\\nhttps://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/issues/21991\\nhttps://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/issues/18556\\nhttps://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/issues/17945\\nhttps://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/issues/14545\\nhttps://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/issues/10623\\n\\n\",\"state\":\"open\",\"html_url\":\"https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/issues/43513\",\"user\":{\"login\":\"javiercn\",\"id\":6995051,\"profile_url\":\"https://github.com/javiercn\",\"avatar_url\":\"https://avatars.githubusercontent.com/u/6995051?v=4\"},\"author_association\":\"MEMBER\",\"labels\":[\"enhancement\",\"area-blazor\",\"feature-blazor-server\",\"Pillar: [2026-08-26T22:05:46.900Z] [DEBUG] [rpc] github←resp 6803b {"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"result":{"_meta":{"io.modelcontextprotocol/serverInfo":{"icons":[{"mimeType":"image/png","src":"data:image/png;base64,","theme":"light"},{"mimeType":"image/png","src":"data:image/png;base64,","theme":"dark"}],"name":"github-mcp-server","title":"GitHub MCP Server","version":"v1.9.0"}},"content":[{"type":"text","text":"{\"number\":67259,\"title\":\"[Blazor WASM] BlazorWasmServiceDefaults template has circular DI dependency in IPostConfigureOptions on .NET 11 preview\",\"body\":\"## Description\\n\\nThe `BlazorWasmServiceDefaults` project template (used for Blazor WebAssembly standalone apps with Aspire) has a circular DI dependency in `Extensions.cs` that causes an `AggregateException(CircularDependencyException)` at runtime on .NET 11 preview 6.\\n\\n## Root Cause\\n\\nIn `Extensions.cs`, the `IPostConfigureOptions` singleton resolves `ILoggerFactory` from the service provider during factory creation:\\n\\n```csharp\\nbuilder.Services.AddSingleton\\u0026gt;(sp =\\u0026gt;\\n{\\n    var logger = sp.GetRequiredService().CreateLogger(\\u0026#34;Aspire.OtlpExport\\u0026#34;);\\n    return new PostConfigureOptions(null, o =\\u0026gt;\\n    {\\n        o.HttpClientFactory = () =\\u0026gt; new HttpClient(new BackgroundExportHandler(pipeline, logger));\\n    });\\n});\\n```\\n\\n### Circular chain:\\n```\\nIPostConfigureOptions (singleton factory)\\n  → ILoggerFactory\\n    → OpenTelemetry LoggerProvider\\n      → OtlpLogExporter\\n        → OtlpExporterOptions\\n          → IOptionsFactory\\n            → IPostConfigureOptions  ← CIRCLE\\n```\\n\\nThe logging OTLP exporter (registered via `logging.AddOtlpExporter(...)`) needs `OtlpExporterOptions`, which triggers `IPostConfigureOptions`, which needs `ILoggerFactory`, which triggers the OTel logger provider creation, which creates the OTLP log exporter → circular.\\n\\n## Reproduction\\n\\n1. Create a new Blazor WebAssembly standalone app with the `blazor-wasm-servicedefaults` template\\n2. Wire it with an Aspire AppHost using `AddBlazorWasmProject` + `AddBlazorGateway` + `WithOtlpExporter`\\n3. Use .NET 11 preview 6 SDK (11.0.100-preview.6.26316.109)\\n4. Navigate to any page in the WASM app\\n5. Browser console shows: `AggregateException_ctor_DefaultMessage (CircularDependencyException, Microsoft.Extensions.Options.IOptionsFactory)`\\n\\n## Environment\\n\\n- .NET SDK: 11.0.100-preview.6.26316.109\\n- Aspire SDK: 13.4.5\\n- OpenTelemetry.Exporter.OpenTelemetryProtocol: 1.15.3\\n- Browser: Chromium (Blazor WebAssembly)\\n\\n## Workaround\\n\\nUse `NullLoggerFactory.Instance` instead of resolving `ILoggerFactory` from DI:\\n\\n```csharp\\nbuilder.Services.AddSingleton\\u0026gt;(_ =\\u0026gt;\\n{\\n    var logger = Microsoft.Extensions.Logging.Abstractions.NullLoggerFactory.Instance\\n        .CreateLogger(\\u0026#34;Aspire.OtlpExport\\u0026#34;);\\n    return new PostConfigureOptions(null, o =\\u0026gt;\\n    {\\n        o.HttpClientFactory = () =\\u0026gt; new HttpClient(new BackgroundExportHandler(pipeline, logger));\\n    });\\n});\\n```\\n\\nThis breaks the circular dependency at the cost of losing export failure logging.\\n\\n## Suggested Fix\\n\\nOptions to fix while preserving logging:\\n1. Use `NullLoggerFactory` as the default, then lazily swap in a real logger after the host is built\\n2. Accept an `ILogger` parameter in `BackgroundExportHandler` that lazily resolves from the service provider on first use\\n3. Register `BackgroundExportHandler` separately and inject a lazy `ILogger`\\n4. Move the `IPostConfigureOptions` registration to run after the OTel logging pipeline is fully wired (deferred configuration)\\n\\n## Affected Template\\n\\n`src/ProjectTemplates/Web.ProjectTemplates/content/BlazorWasmServiceDefaults-CSharp/Extensions.cs`\\n\\n(Also affects the playground sample at `playground/BlazorStandalone/BlazorStandalone.ClientServiceDefaults/Extensions.cs` in `dotnet/aspire`)\\n\",\"state\":\"closed\",\"state_reason\":\"completed\",\"html_url\":\"https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/issues/67259\",\"user\":{\"login\":\"javiercn\",\"id\":6995051,\"profile_url\":\"https://github.com/javiercn\",\"avatar_url\":\"https://avatars.githubusercontent.com/u/6995051?v=4\"},\"author_association\":\"MEMBER\",\"labels\":[\"bug\",\"area-blazor\",\"feature-templates\"],\"assignees\":[\"javiercn\",\"Copilot\"],\"milestone\":\"11.0-preview7\",\"comments\":8,\"reactions\":{\"total_count\":1,\"+1\":0,\"-1\":0,\"laugh\":0,\"confused\":0,\"heart\":0,\"hooray\":0,\"rocket\":0,\"eyes\":1},\"created_at\":\"2026-06-17T11:37:23Z\",\"updated_at\":\"2026-07-27T13:38:46Z\",\"closed_at\":\"2026-07-27T13:38:46Z\",\"closed_by\":\"javiercn\",\"issue_type\":\"Bug\",\"has_parent\":false,\"has_children\":false,\"closed_by_pull_requests\":{\"total_count\":0,\"references\":[]}}"}],"resultType":"complete"}}

[2026-08-26T22:05:48.510Z] [DEBUG] [rpc] github←resp 5870b {"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"result":{"_meta":{"io.modelcontextprotocol/serverInfo":{"icons":[{"mimeType":"image/png","src":"data:image/png;base64,","theme":"light"},{"mimeType":"image/png","src":"data:image/png;base64,","theme":"dark"}],"name":"github-mcp-server","title":"GitHub MCP Server","version":"v1.9.0"}},"content":[{"type":"text","text":"{\"number\":68801,\"title\":\"Remove the Blazor WebAssembly Service Defaults OTLP export workaround after OpenTelemetry supports async export\",\"body\":\"### Description\\n\\nThe Blazor WebAssembly Service Defaults template currently uses `BackgroundExportHandler` to work around synchronous OTLP export on single-threaded WebAssembly.\\n\\nOpenTelemetry\\u0026#39;s OTLP exporter calls:\\n\\n```csharp\\nHttpClient.SendAsync(...).GetAwaiter().GetResult()\\n```\\n\\nThis can stall when the HTTP pipeline performs asynchronous work. The template handler avoids that stall by capturing the request, immediately returning a synthetic successful response, and sending the real request asynchronously through a Polly resilience pipeline.\\n\\nOpenTelemetry added task-based batch and metric workers for single-threaded WebAssembly in open-telemetry/opentelemetry-dotnet#6379, but the worker still invokes the synchronous exporter contract. The remaining limitation is tracked by open-telemetry/opentelemetry-dotnet#7708.\\n\\nOnce that issue is resolved and the fix is available in a stable OpenTelemetry release, remove the template workaround and use the standard OTLP exporter implementation.\\n\\n### Proposed changes\\n\\n- Update the Blazor WebAssembly Service Defaults OpenTelemetry dependencies to a stable version containing the fix for open-telemetry/opentelemetry-dotnet#7708.\\n- Delete `BackgroundExportHandler.cs`.\\n- Remove the custom `IPostConfigureOptions` configuration that supplies `BackgroundExportHandler`.\\n- Remove the custom `ResiliencePipelineBuilder` configuration.\\n- Remove the `Microsoft.Extensions.Http.Resilience` dependency if it is no longer otherwise needed.\\n- Configure logs, traces, and metrics using the standard `AddOtlpExporter` APIs.\\n- Allow OTLP exporters to use the normal HTTP client integration without bypassing globally configured asynchronous handlers such as service discovery.\\n\\n### Validation\\n\\nAdd or update browser integration coverage to verify that, in single-threaded Blazor WebAssembly:\\n\\n- Logs, traces, and metrics are exported successfully over OTLP/HTTP.\\n- Export works when `IHttpClientFactory` includes an asynchronous delegating handler, including the globally configured service-discovery handler used by the template.\\n- Export requests are not reported as successful before the HTTP operation completes.\\n- Export failures are surfaced through normal OpenTelemetry diagnostics.\\n- Retry, timeout, flush, and shutdown behavior use OpenTelemetry\\u0026#39;s standard semantics without fire-and-forget requests.\\n- No provider must be manually resolved to initialize OpenTelemetry; normal `IHostedService` startup remains sufficient.\\n\\n### Dependencies\\n\\nBlocked by:\\n\\n- open-telemetry/opentelemetry-dotnet#7708\\n\\nRelated:\\n\\n- #64574\\n- #64890\\n- #67259\\n- #67267\\n\",\"state\":\"open\",\"html_url\":\"https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/issues/68801\",\"user\":{\"login\":\"danroth27\",\"id\":1874516,\"profile_url\":\"https://github.com/danroth27\",\"avatar_url\":\"https://avatars.githubusercontent.com/u/1874516?v=4\"},\"author_association\":\"MEMBER\",\"labels\":[\"area-blazor\"],\"comments\":1,\"reactions\":{\"total_count\":0,\"+1\":0,\"-1\":0,\"laugh\":0,\"confused\":0,\"heart\":0,\"hooray\":0,\"rocket\":0,\"eyes\":0},\"created_at\":\"2026-08-26T11:52:00Z\",\"updated_at\":\"2026-08-26T11:56:38Z\",\"issue_type\":\"Feature\",\"has_parent\":false,\"has_children\":false,\"closed_by_pull_requests\":{\"total_count\":0,\"references\":[]}}"}],"resultType":"complete"}}

For example:\\n\\n * Render batches are communicated to JS via zero-copy shared memory rather than by serialization\\n * Events triggered from JS are always processed synchronously by .NET, so there\\u0026#39;s no need to queue them\\n\\nAt first glance, it appears to work with `true`, but that\\u0026#39;s a mirage: it does *not* guarantee correctness in that mode, because the core single-threadedness assumption is violated. For example, JS might raise event 2 before event 1 finished processing, and by the time event 1 is done, there might not even be an event 2 handler any more and then you have an error.\\n\\n### Why we\\u0026#39;re only just encountering this now\\n\\n1. We didn\\u0026#39;t have multithreading before\\n2. Even to the extent that we did have an early preview of multithreading, it worked by running .NET on the browser UI thread, so we could define that as the sync context and then all the same assumptions would remain valid within that sync context. But now .NET WebAssembly has just moved to the new \\u0026#34;deputy thread\\u0026#34; multithreading model (i.e., all .NET code is on a background worker), these assumptions are no longer valid (e.g., because the UI thread\\u0026#39;s JS can no longer communicate with .NET in a synchronous, blocking manner).\\n\\n### Ensuring correctness\\n\\nWe\\u0026#39;ve already solved all these problems in our other hosting environments, Server and WebView, because they\\u0026#39;ve always been innately asynchronous from the beginning. We would need to generalize/port all these mechanisms so they are shared with or copied by the WebAssembly renderer, JS interop, eventing system, etc.:\\n\\n- [ ] Change rendering to serialize renderbatches to JS instead of doing shared-memory reads\\n- [ ] Change the rendering flow so that the renderer\\u0026#39;s `UpdateDisplayAsync` returns a `Task` that doesn\\u0026#39;t complete until the JS side sends back an explicit acknowledgement of that renderbatch\\n- [ ] Review JS interop to make sure any low-level assumptions we\\u0026#39;ve made about synchrony during the internals of message passing are replaced by async assumptions\\n- [ ] Do the above without changing things for the **single-threaded** WebAssembly flavour, since (1) it would be breaking if for example synchronous UI updates became async, and (2) those perf optimizations are there for a reason, and we don\\u0026#39;t want to make rendering many times more expensive in cases where you\\u0026#39;d be serializing huge strings, for example. It\\u0026#39;s OK to have significant behavioral and performance changes when people opt into multithreading, but not when they don\\u0026#39;t.\\n\\n### Approach\\n\\nAs a broad strategy, I think we can:\\n\\n * Factor out some new `WebRenderer` subclass called something like `AsyncWebRenderer` that holds the common logic around serializing renderbatches and accepting the async renderbatch acknowledgements from JS. This can then be used by all of Server, WebView, and multithreaded-WebAssembly.\\n * Use our WebView implementation as the reference for how a complete, async-safe rendering and eventing model should work, because this was more recently implemented than Server and is generally simpler and cleaner. There\\u0026#39;s not a huge amount of code in it, really. If some extra work is needed to queue event notifications, for example, we should see that clearly from the WebView code.\\n\\nI suspect it\\u0026#39;s not necessary to have two different builds of `Microsoft.AspNetCore.Components.WebAssembly`. The total amount of code that should differ between the threaded and not-threaded won\\u0026#39;t be very much. I expect we can just have two different `Renderer` subclasses and some if/else branches in the JS code.\",\"state\":\"open\",\"html_url\":\"https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/issues/54365\",\"user\":{\"login\":\"SteveSandersonMS\",\"id\":1101362,\"profile_url\":\"https://github.com/SteveSandersonMS\",\"avatar_url\":\"https://avatars.githubusercontent.com/u/1101362?v=4\"},\"author_association\":\"MEMBER\",\"labels\":[\"enhancement\",\"area-blazor\",\"triaged\",\"feature-blazor-wasm-threading\"],\"milestone\":\"Backlog\",\"comments\":26,\"reactions\":{\"total_count\":47,\"+1\":30,\"-1\":0,\"laugh\":0,\"confused\":0,\"heart\":17,\"hooray\":0,\"rocket\":0,\"eyes\":0},\"created_at\":\"2024-03-05T10:02:51Z\",\"updated_at\":\"2026-04-21T00:06:24Z\",\"issue_type\":\"Feature\",\"has_parent\":true,\"has_children\":false,\"parent\":{\"number\":17730,\"title\":\"Real multithreading in Blazor WebAssembly\",\"state\":\"OPEN\",\"url\":\"https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/issues/17730\",\"repository\":\"dotnet/aspnetcore\"},\"closed_by_pull_requests\":{\"total_count\":0,\"references\":[]}}"}],"resultType":"complete"}}

Our application handles large datasets (e.g., 10,000 records), and during export operations, the entire web page becomes unresponsive, preventing any further user interaction until the export completes.\\n\\nIn Blazor Server, we have successfully maintained UI responsiveness by utilizing multi-threading with Task.Run, as shown below:\\n\\n**Before:**\\n\\n`csharp\\n\\nawait ExportHelper(GridModel, DataSource);\\nusing MemoryStream outputStream = new MemoryStream();\\n_workbook.Save(outputStream, IsCsvExport);\\n`\\n\\n**After:**\\n\\n`csharp\\n\\nawait Task.Run(() =\\u0026gt; ExportHelper(GridModel, DataSource)).ConfigureAwait(false);\\n\\nusing MemoryStream outputStream = new MemoryStream();\\n\\nawait Task.Run(() =\\u0026gt; _workbook.Save(outputStream, IsCsvExport)).ConfigureAwait(false);`\\n\\nWhile this approach works effectively in Blazor Server, it does not yield the same results in Blazor WebAssembly. The single-threaded nature of WebAssembly causes the export operation to block the UI thread, rendering the page unresponsive.\\n\\nWe have attempted to split the data source and apply Task.Yield in WebAssembly to enhance responsiveness, but these efforts have not been successful.\\n\\n### Expected Behavior\\n\\nWe aim to achieve similar UI responsiveness in Blazor WebAssembly as we experience in Blazor Server, allowing users to interact with the page during export operations.\\n\\nRequest:\\n\\nWe kindly request consideration for adding support for responsive, non-blocking long-running tasks (e.g., data exports) in Blazor WebAssembly. This enhancement would enable us to maintain an interactive UI for end-users.\\n\\n**Environment Details:**\\n\\nDevice: DELL Latitude 3410\\nBrowser: Chrome\\nBlazor WebAssembly Version: 8.0.0\\n\\n### .NET Version\\n\\nBlazor WebAssembly Version: 8.0.0\\n\",\"state\":\"closed\",\"state_reason\":\"completed\",\"html_url\":\"https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/issues/58836\",\"user\":{\"login\":\"DhivyaRajendran\",\"id\":24690158,\"profile_url\":\"https://github.com/DhivyaRajendran\",\"avatar_url\":\"https://avatars.githubusercontent.com/u/24690158?v=4\"},\"author_association\":\"NONE\",\"labels\":[\"Needs: Author Feedback\",\"area-blazor\",\"Status: No Recent Activity\"],\"comments\":3,\"reactions\":{\"total_count\":0,\"+1\":0,\"-1\":0,\"laugh\":0,\"confused\":0,\"heart\":0,\"hooray\":0,\"rocket\":0,\"eyes\":0},\"created_at\":\"2024-11-08T06:03:14Z\",\"updated_at\":\"2024-11-18T00:35:16Z\",\"closed_at\":\"2024-11-18T00:35:16Z\",\"closed_by\":\"dotnet-policy-service[bot]\",\"has_parent\":false,\"has_children\":false,\"closed_by_pull_requests\":{\"total_count\":0,\"references\":[]}}"}],"resultType":"complete"}}

It\\u0026#39;s now pretty easy to enable and use - people just need to:\\n\\n A. Add `true` in the wasm project `csproj`\\n\\n B. Ensure the site is served with the relevant `Cross-Origin-...` headers as per [browser requirements](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/JavaScript/Reference/Global_Objects/SharedArrayBuffer#security_requirements)\\n  * For Blazor WebAssembly Standalone, during development the dev server will automatically serve these headers based on `WasmEnableThreads` (because there\\u0026#39;s no easy way to configure the dev server, so we have to do it automatically). And in production, the developer has to configure the server\\u0026#39;s response headers themselves because Blazor/ASP.NETCore is not involved. **This PR does not affect it.**\\n  * For traditional Blazor WebAssembly hosted-on-ASP.NET-Core (i.e., using `MapBlazorFrameworkFiles` and `MapFallbackToFile`, *not* the new .NET 8 Blazor Web model), developers can easily write a few lines of ASP.NET Core middleware to serve the necessary headers, which we can document. **This PR does not affect it.**\\n  * For Blazor Web using the `InteractiveWebAssembly` render mode, **this PR adds a simple API for serving the headers** on the correct endpoints matching what gets registered by `MapRazorComponents`. That is, it serves them for any Razor Components endpoint (since it may be or contain an `InteractiveWebAssembly` component), plus for `_framework/*` (since that\\u0026#39;s required to load the Blazor WebAssembly runtime with SharedArrayBuffer support in the worker thread).\\n\\n## Proposed API\\n\\n```diff\\nnamespace Microsoft.AspNetCore.Components.WebAssembly.Server;\\n\\npublic sealed class WebAssemblyComponentsEndpointOptions\\n{\\n+    /// \\n+    /// Gets or sets a flag to determine whether to enable WebAssembly multithreading. If true,\\n+    /// the server will add headers similar to \\u003ccode\\u003eCross-Origin-Embedder-Policy: require-corp\\u003c/code\\u003e and\\n+    /// \\u003ccode\\u003eCross-Origin-Opener-Policy: same-origin\\u003c/code\\u003e on the response for the host page, because\\n+    /// this is required to enable the SharedArrayBuffer feature in the browser.\\n+    ///\\n+    /// Note that enabling this feature can restrict your ability to use other JavaScript APIs. For more\\n+    /// information, see .\\n+    /// \\n+    public bool ServeMultithreadingHeaders { get; set; }\\n}\\n```\\n\\n## Usage Examples\\n\\n```cs\\napp.MapRazorComponents()\\n    .AddInteractiveWebAssemblyRenderMode(options =\\u0026gt; { options.ServeMultithreadingHeaders = true; })\\n    .AddAdditionalAssemblies(typeof(MyWebAssemblyApp.Pages.Index).Assembly);\\n```\\n\\n## Alternative Designs\\n\\nOverall, since this feature is nascent and remains experimental, I\\u0026#39;m erring on the side of making it more explicit and literal so people who turn it on know what they are getting into. In the future if we get to the point that wasm multithreading is so good that most people should enable it, we retain the option to streamline the usage.\\n\\n### Alternative: Infer it automatically\\n\\nWe could try to infer this based on `` in the wasm csproj, but:\\n\\n1. There could be multiple wasm apps. What if they want different configurations?\\n2. Since this is an early and quite experimental feature, it\\u0026#39;s really good to force developers to opt in to serving the COOP headers explicitly. Doing so can restrict the availability of other JS APIs (e.g., can interfere with popups that might be used for auth flows) as described at https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/JavaScript/Reference/Global_Objects/SharedArrayBuffer#security_requirements. It might turn out to be fine, but in case this causes issues for people, it\\u0026#39;s really good that the developer has a chance to discover what they are enabling and the possible side-effects of that.\\n\\n### Alternative: Extension method\\n\\nAn alternative API would be making it an extension method on `RazorComponentsEndpointConventionBuilder`, e.g.:\\n\\n    app.MapRazorComponents().AddInteractiveWebAssemblyRenderMode().ServeWasmMultithreadingHeaders();\\n\\n... but that would be very strange and ambiguous since you could also write:\\n\\n    app.MapRazorComponents().AddInteractiveServerRenderMode().ServeWasmMultithreadingHeaders();\\n\\nI prefer it being an option on `AddInteractiveWebAssemblyRenderMode` since it is more specific and accurate, as it only applies within that case.\\n\\n### Alternative: Naming\\n\\nIt would be more obvious to call it `EnableMultithreading` instead of `ServeMultithreadingHeaders`, but that would not so well serve the purpose of helping developer understand what exactly they are enabling and how it might have other side effects.\\n\\n## Risks\\n\\nNothing obvious.\",\"state\":\"closed\",\"state_reason\":\"completed\",\"html_url\":\"https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/issues/54071\",\"user\":{\"login\":\"SteveSandersonMS\",\"id\":1101362,\"profile_url\":\"https://github.com/SteveSandersonMS\",\"avatar_url\":\"https://avatars.githubusercontent.com/u/1101362?v=4\"},\"author_association\":\"MEMBER\",\"labels\":[\"area-blazor\",\"api-approved\"],\"assignees\":[\"SteveSandersonMS\"],\"milestone\":\"9.0-preview3\",\"comments\":6,\"reactions\":{\"total_count\":2,\"+1\":2,\"-1\":0,\"laugh\":0,\"confused\":0,\"heart\":0,\"hooray\":0,\"rocket\":0,\"eyes\":0},\"created_at\":\"2024-02-16T13:47:36Z\",\"updated_at\":\"2024-03-04T09:27:33Z\",\"closed_at\":\"2024-03-04T09:27:33Z\",\"closed_by\":\"SteveSandersonMS\",\"has_parent\":false,\"has_children\":false,\"closed_by_pull_requests\":{\"total_count\":0,\"references\":[]}}"}],"resultType":"complete"}}

This is because it came in very late in the release cycle and doesn’t yet do the caching that it needs to do, so we wanted to avoid impacting developers who aren’t using workloads.  This issue tracks the remaining work.\\n \\nTo enable the workload resolver, you can either set the `MSBuildEnableWorkloadResolver` environment variable to true, or create a file named EnableWorkloadResolver.sentinel next to the workload resolver DLL.  The DLL used will be different for full Framework MSBuild (which is used in Visual Studio and “msbuild” on the command line) and .NET Core MSBuild (which is used by the dotnet CLI).  So you will need to create the file in two places if you want to enable the workload resolver that way.  The DLL paths will be similar to the following (with highlighted parts likely to change):\\n \\n•\\tC:\\\\Program Files (x86)\\\\Microsoft Visual Studio\\\\2019\\\\Preview\\\\MSBuild\\\\Current\\\\Bin\\\\SdkResolvers\\\\Microsoft.DotNet.MSBuildSdkResolver\\\\Microsoft.DotNet.MSBuildSdkResolver.dll\\n•\\tC:\\\\Program Files\\\\dotnet\\\\sdk\\\\5.0.100\\\\Microsoft.NET.Sdk.WorkloadMSBuildSdkResolver.dll\\n \\nAdditionally (whether you enable the workload resolver via the environment variable or a sentinel file), you will need to copy Newtonsoft.Json.dll version 11.0 to the folder with the full framework MSBuild SDK resolver.  You should be able to download the package here and extract the DLL from the lib\\\\net45 folder.  We plan to fix this for the GA release of VS 16.8.\\n \\n### Creating a workload\\n \\nThere is a very simple workload in the dotnet/sdk repo that is used for testing the workload features: https://github.com/dotnet/sdk/blob/release/5.0.1xx/src/Assets/TestWorkloads/manifests/Microsoft.NET.Sdk.TestWorkload/WorkloadManifest.json.  You can refer to / modify that workload, and refer to the Workload Resolvers design doc for overall guidance.\\n\",\"state\":\"closed\",\"state_reason\":\"completed\",\"locked\":true,\"html_url\":\"https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/issues/29499\",\"user\":{\"login\":\"pranavkm\",\"id\":174281,\"profile_url\":\"https://github.com/pranavkm\",\"avatar_url\":\"https://avatars.githubusercontent.com/u/174281?v=4\"},\"author_association\":\"CONTRIBUTOR\",\"labels\":[\"Done\",\"enhancement\",\"area-blazor\",\"severity-blocking\",\"affected-medium\"],\"assignees\":[\"pranavkm\"],\"milestone\":\"6.0-preview2\",\"comments\":2,\"reactions\":{\"total_count\":0,\"+1\":0,\"-1\":0,\"laugh\":0,\"confused\":0,\"heart\":0,\"hooray\":0,\"rocket\":0,\"eyes\":0},\"created_at\":\"2021-01-21T16:16:10Z\",\"updated_at\":\"2021-03-25T22:01:17Z\",\"closed_at\":\"2021-02-23T21:14:16Z\",\"closed_by\":\"pranavkm\",\"has_parent\":false,\"has_children\":false,\"closed_by_pull_requests\":{\"total_count\":0,\"references\":[]}}"}],"resultType":"complete"}}
